newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr as RBI, SBI stay away.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr as RBI, SBI stay away.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended Thursday up against the dollar at 35.765/775 on poor demand for the U.S. currency, dealers said.
They said the rupee moved up as there was no demand from either the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) or the State Bank of India (SBI), traditionally the largets dollar buyer in the market.
The rupee traded at a high of 35.7675 and a low of 35.7925, with most of the day's trade between 35.775 and 35.785, dealers said.
Dealers said the premiums on forward dollars ended almost unchanged from the previous day's close.

"Exporters are looking to sell far forwards but there are few buyers around at the moment," said a dealer. "With the rupee either steady or moving up, there is little incentive for importers to cover."
"There was some selling in cash-spot today as tomorrow is a reporting Friday and a strike has also been called for by trade unions," said another dealer.
Trade unions have called for a strike on Friday and bankers said banking operations will be affected if the strike takes place.
"Technically since only one section, the clerical staff, is on strike, banks will not be closed," said a dealer. "But for all practical purposes, operations will be crippled tomorrow."
Dealers said the annualised premium on six-month dollars ended Thursday steady at around 3.4 percent.
